[Alrighty! Let's get the ball rolling in here. It's been a while, but I think I have a short story in me.]

"Come here child, sit down by the fire. Mind the rats this time, if you knock them over again your mother with have your hide up on the walls."

The smell of smoke, charred wood, and cooking rat hangs heavy in the air. The lack of airflow in the cave forces the smells to linger and intertwine.

"You wanted to hear a story, so I will tell you one. You are older now, this story will be different. No more fantasies, no more tales. Your parents don't agree with me, but I am your grandfather and keeper of this story. I will decide when it is time"

A log, as wide as the breath of a hand glowed brightly with the heat of ember in it's heart. It glowed strong, casting it's light across the the stone walls of the cave. Wooden racks project dancing shadows all around the open space of the cave mouth.

"You live in a world of dust and strife child. But know, the world was not always so. The world was once much brighter. This is the story of the world that once was. Listen to me, and remember my words well, for when I die, this story will be yours to tell. You must not let it fade away, like the sunlight at night. This is the story of our past, our people."

Dust and dirt shifted outside of the cave mouth. A small lizard picked it's way carefully among the rocks. One head lapping at the air, then the other. It moved with purpose towards the scraps of past meals. Using it's needle sharp teeth, it nabbed a piece of rat hide and carried it quickly off into the darkness.

"A time, many years past, our world was once green and full of life. Water flow freely and there was enough food for each man. People lived in structures, not caves, and there were even places where many buildings were collected together. These places where called 'cities'. Some people even lived their whole lives without ever leaving some of the larger cities. There was violence and wars back then, but not like the horrid things that we see today. A man could travel alone, and unarmed in those days, without fear of being killed and eaten."

The embers of the fire crushed and billowed as another log was thrown on top.

"The world was bright and alive. But then the world started to die. We humans killed it. We not only killed our planet, but we killed ourselves. Billions of us died during the Exodus War. Not just warriors, but normal people to. Men, women, children. The few in power, the few that had large amounts of a thing called currency, thought that our world's problems could be solved if there we less people. They started killing anyone who wasn't apart of their cabal of evil. People fought back, and quickly as well. But it wasn't enough. The Purge soon became the Exodus War. The rich held off the poor while they built ships to flee the planet. The war was to much for our world, and it gave up the last of the life it had. This is was cause this barren, lifeless world you live in child."

An old, leather bound book shined near the fire. It's age belied the youthful vigor it radiated. It's cover glowing as if it was given new life.

"Now you parents may have been right. You are younger than you would be to hear this story. But things have changed. You did well bringing your grandfather that book. Tomorrow will be a big day for you boy. Tomorrow the whole family is leaving this cave. I will need you to help everyone pack our belongings. You will even get your first rifle once we leave."

The old man lovingly picks up the leather book. He holds it dearly in his hands.

"Tomorrow, boy, tomorrow we're going to see the White Castle."
